speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In my speech, I will touch on three areas: one, how the work of food charities in Singapore fits with our social compact; two, how the Bill will support their work; and finally, how, as a society, we can join hands across Government, community and businesses to support more intentional giving.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Food support organisations play an important role in our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They are a positive model of how community partners with families and the Government and exemplify our "many helping hands" approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In Singapore, we encourage self-reliance and family support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Individuals do their best for themselves and their families and families provide the first line of support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The next layer of support is a caring community, comprising neighbours, community organisations and other partners, including corporates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Members of the community, like our food support organisations, contribute their time, resources and expertise and help create opportunities for those they help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government helps to create conditions and opportunities for Singaporeans to provide a better life for themselves and their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On occasion, some families fall on hard times for a variety of reasons and the Government steps in to provide support, in essence, provide a social safety net to help them regain stability and self-reliance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Thus, food charities do not work alone, but alongside many others who seek to help individuals and families in need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Together, they provide a wide range of food support, such as cooking and delivering hot meals, distributing dry rations, setting up community shops, as well as providing digital credits that allow beneficiaries to select the food that best meets their dietary requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Food charities complement the Government's support, by offering additional aid and expanding the range of choices for families in need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Their efforts go a long way in helping to alleviate the burdens of these families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They are often unsung heroes, operating behind the scenes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many food charities and their dedicated volunteers work tirelessly around the clock, including at night and in the wee hours of the morning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They collect donated food, prepare and repack them for their beneficiaries and help prepare cooked meals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many also work closely with social services to identify needy families and make plans for supporting them, in line with their needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I have had the privilege of leading the Charity Food Workgroup, or CFWG, over the past four years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our goal is to bring partners within the food donation ecosystem together so that we can harness our collective strengths to practise "good giving and giving right".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have done this by: (a) helping those in need identify and receive food support; (b) reducing duplication of food support and reducing food wastage through better coordination; and (c) encouraging better giving through a shared emphasis on providing food support that meets beneficiaries' dietary needs and in a way that gives beneficiaries greater choice and dignity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The CFWG's work is beneficiary-centric and largely driven by the food charities which are the key enablers of these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The workgroup has also risen to the occasion during difficult times.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: During the circuit breaker, the work of many food charities was disrupted, with many unable to operate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Recognising that there was higher demand for food support then, CFWG members rallied together and developed a central repository of food support beneficiaries' data.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This enabled charities that were still able to operate to take over to provide support to those who needed help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we continue to encourage more food charities to come on board the database.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have also launched a FoodConnect Directory that enables families to access food charities according to where they live and their dietary requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This has helped families more easily find food support that best meets their needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Directory has become more comprehensive over time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, it includes food charities offering halal, non-halal and vegetarian food support options in all service regions in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Bill reflects the collective efforts of stakeholders in the food donation space who have come together to think about how to incentivise food donation and reduce food wastage in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We welcome the protections conferred by the Bill, as more donors can confidently participate in food donation and less food will go to waste.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through our food charities and food support organisations stepping in to organise these donations, more food can be given to those in need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And organisations can also benefit from the assurance that there are legislative protections in place, as they carry out their work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I hope that, collectively, these measures will help encourage greater community giving while, at the same time, reducing food wastage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) supports the spirit of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: My hope is that this will lead to greater choice and dignity for beneficiaries of food support, who will be better placed to get food support that best meets their needs and preferences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also encourage donors and food charities to work with CFWG and, together, we can address the community's needs more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For our beneficiaries to have the option of choice is not simply or merely about preferences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I have a four-year-old boy at home, so, I know for young children, having a choice over food options not only helps them feel like they have some control over their lives, but learning to decide is also a key part of growing up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And yet, for others, being able to choose the food that they eat comes from a position of need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And for that, I salute all who have been, and will continue, to be hard at work in our food charities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Reducing food waste helps us realise our vision of a zero-waste nation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We support the GSFD Bill as we believe it will help reduce food waste by facilitating the donation of surplus food to beneficiaries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The preferred way to manage food waste is to avoid food production in excess of consumption at the onset.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We encourage all food establishments, including manufacturers, caterers and retailers, to review processes and practices, to reduce the incidence of excessive food production upstream.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Stakeholders may consult the food waste minimisation guidebooks available on the NEA and SFA websites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Where there is unsold or excess food, we support food donation as a possible avenue to reduce wastage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The GSFD Bill thus complements existing efforts to reduce food waste by facilitating food donation which would then avoid the need for food waste treatment and its associated operational costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Hazel Poa, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Jean See, Miss Rachel Ong and Ms Joan Pereira suggested further measures to encourage food waste reduction through food donations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We thank the Members for their suggestions and will study them further together with MSF as they continue to look at ways to strengthen efforts in the food support space.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As we facilitate and support measures that reduce food waste, we must also ensure that the donated food is safe and suitable for our consumption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Don Wee and Mr Gan Thiam Poh spoke about food safety risks and the importance of ensuring that donors with ill intentions do not misuse the protection accorded by the GSFD Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Bill aligns with MSE and SFA's approach to assure food safety and strikes a balance of roles and responsibilities among various parties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It makes clear that the safety of donated food is a joint responsibility of the Government, food donors, intermediaries, such food distribution organisations, and consumers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MSE and SFA are responsible for establishing the regulatory framework for food safety and providing an enabling environment for the food industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Don Wee, Ms Hany Soh and Mr Edward Chia mentioned the need for clear guidelines and standards to guide food donors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about how we could ensure that food donors are well-informed and fully compliant with existing food safety and hygiene regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since 2021, SFA has published a set of guidelines for food safety practices during the preparation, delivery, storage and distribution of food for charitable causes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These guidelines are refreshed periodically to ensure their continued relevance to food donors and food distribution organisations, and they are available online.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Don Wee, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Zhulkarnain and Ms Ng Ling Ling also mentioned other measures to ensure that food donors maintain proper food safety standards, such as the need for training of staff and volunteers, maintaining records for accountability and tracing, and regular inspections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These are good food safety practices which SFA will continue to raise awareness of and educate the food industry, food distribution organisations and consumers on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Where feedback is received and preliminary checks suggest food safety lapses, SFA will also utilise its levers, including inspection, sampling and testing, to investigate and take action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Food donors and food distribution organisations continue to have a responsibility to ensure the safety of the food they are donating or distributing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, premises and equipment for food preparation and distribution should be kept clean and well-maintained, and employees and volunteers handling the food should adopt good hygiene practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Recipients should also be advised by food donors and food distribution organisations on measures they could take to ensure food safety, such as checking the condition of food upon receipt and consuming it within the recommended timeline.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: First, the food should not have been unsafe and not unsuitable at the time it left possession and control of the food donor.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Second, the food donor should have informed the recipient of any food handling requirements to ensure that the donated food remained safe and suitable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Third, the food donor should have informed the recipient of any time beyond which the food would no longer have remained safe and suitable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last, the food donor should have taken all reasonably practicable measures to comply with any applicable requirement under any written law related to food safety and hygiene when handling the food to be donated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These conditions provide clarity to donors on the requirements that they should meet in order to be eligible for protection from any criminal or civil liability arising from food safety incidents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The conditions thus provide assurance to food donation recipients that donors would have taken necessary measures to safeguard the safety of the food they provide.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Recipients of donated food also have a part to play to ensure food safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They should exercise due diligence and take responsibility in noting the information provided by donors or food distribution organisations so that the donated food remains safe and suitable to consume.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While the Bill facilitates food donation, it does not impede SFA's responsibilities as a regulator or its ability to investigate food safety lapses and take action against non-compliance with food safety directions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about MSE and SFA's enforcement and investigation processes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also enquired on what would happen when donors do not follow safety guidelines.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Director General (Food Administration) can issue directions to suspend food donation or distribution activities until appropriate rectification has been done.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked whether intermediary food rescue groups would be held liable if food was found to be unsuitable and unsafe.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Bill covers all food donors, including food distribution organisations such as food charities, which distribute food donated by others for charitable purpose.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: If the donor or food distribution organisation is found to have donated or distributed unsafe or unsuitable food or did not take reasonable measures to ensure food safety, they would not be protected from liability under the GSFD Bill as they would have failed to meet the conditions stipulated in the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SFA will continue to be judicious in its investigations and will only take action against the errant party.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, if a food distribution organisation had done its due diligence to ensure the food was safe and suitable when it left its possession, but unknowingly passed on erroneous information from the food donor, the donor would be held responsible while the food distribution organisation will continue to enjoy the protection under the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As announced earlier this year, the FSSB will bring together food safety and security legislation from eight existing Acts into one single Act and provide an overarching framework to ensure coherence across the entire food value chain.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are currently engaging and consulting relevant stakeholders on FSSB.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Yip Hon Weng spoke about the importance of clear and accurate labels on donated food, containing information such as the presence of cooked food and allergens.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These are current requirements for food that is sold, which we are looking to extend to all food, whether sold or donated, under the FSSB.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill will complement the upcoming FSSB by requiring food donors and food distribution organisations to comply with prevailing food safety requirements before protection from criminal and civil liability can apply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To conclude, the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill will help encourage donation of surplus food and contribute to reducing food waste.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Importantly, this will be conducted in a manner that does not compromise food safety and consumer health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It also provides assurance to food donation recipients that reasonable measures have been taken to ensure food safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On that note, my Ministry and I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This might be the shortest Bill with the most number of speakers – 17 Members spoke on our eight-page Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One of our main aims was not just to pass legislation to waive liability for food donations but to shine a spotlight on this very important issue which is seldom debated in this House.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad to say we have achieved this through the debate we had over the past two days.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Allow me some time to now address key points and questions Members have raised.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will also address some of the key concerns that were raised to the Good Samaritan Legislation Review Committee through our consultations with stakeholders and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will also explain why some suggestions raised to the Committee have not been incorporated into the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng just shared, food waste reduction helps us to realise our vision of a zero-waste nation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua also shared that this Bill embodies the spirit of a caring society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should stress that more importantly, the waiver of liability is just one piece of the broader food donation ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are many other things we can, should and must do to encourage food donation beyond this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With these goals in mind, I will provide some clarification on the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members have raised several issues and I have grouped this reply into six areas of concern: one, the unintended and opposite effect of the Bill; two, who is covered under the Bill; three, meeting the four conditions; four, support and help for food donors; five, support and help for recipients; and six, public education and partnerships Let me start by addressing one of the most common feedback we have received.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The elephant in the room is whether this Bill might have the unintended and opposite effect of chilling food donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a big elephant and as we learnt from Ms Poh Li San today, an elephant can weigh up to six tonnes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There were concerns about whether this Bill will make some food donation activities illegal or whether existing food donors will be dissuaded because compliance with the four conditions is too difficult.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill should not make it more onerous for donors to donate food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What it does is to strike a balance between encouraging food donation and at the same time, safeguarding food safety and hygiene standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is about striking the balance between responsibility and philanthropy that Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim so rightly said.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We aim to inspire more food donations and we are confident of achieving this through this Bill without compromising food safety and hygiene standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Ms Jean See shared, the well-being of recipients of donated food is priority.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Committee intended for the definition of a food donor to be as broad as possible to cover as many food donation activities as possible.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For this reason, the Bill does not differentiate between an individual, a community food rescue group, a religious organisation, a business or a registered food charity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NTUC FairPrice asked to clarify if a co-operative society is included in the definition of an "entity".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members of the public and Members here, including Mr Yip Hon Weng and Miss Rachel Ong, asked about the donation of food past the "expiry", "best before" and "use by" dates.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Committee debated this issue extensively but ultimately, one is not allowed to sell food past the "expiry", "best before" and "use by" dates.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Taking that into account, we should not waive liability when one donates the same food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If it is illegal for sale, the Committee felt it would not be appropriate for donation of the same food to be protected from liability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should add that Singapore currently takes a relatively simple approach where "expiry", "best before", "use by" and all other dates are treated the same.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do note that there is room to debate this issue further, especially for the "best before" date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand MSE is studying this issue further and I eagerly await an update.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Mr Yip Hon Weng asked for greater clarity on the Bill's stance on community fridges and food rescue initiatives and whether the Bill extends liability protection to them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was also raised at the second public consultation by Ms Robin, a zero waste advocate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That said, the Committee acknowledges that it may be more difficult for donors or groups involved in community fridges to meet the four conditions since there might not be any direct communication or even face-to-face meetings between the donor and recipient.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For community fridges, there are times we might not even know who the food donor is.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Food rescue initiatives, on the other hand, can more easily meet the four conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For the past few years, we have a monthly food rescue initiative in Nee Soon East.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have spoken to the team managing the food rescue and we are confident we can meet the four conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, during the first public consultation, the Committee surveyed the public on exempting logistics providers from liability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, if our initial legislative efforts are successful in encouraging food donation, future amendments to expand the law to cover logistics providers is a possibility.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, on the definition of food donation, the Committee wanted to ensure that the focus of the Bill remains on charitable giving.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To be considered a donation, the food must be given without payment to the donor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This includes any nominal sum or logistics fee.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If in exchange for the food donation, the donor receives non-monetary benefits, such as publicity, the food given will still be considered a food donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked if the Bill covers donors who receive monetary donations from the public who collect donated food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, if the recipient is the one providing the monetary donation, this is akin to a pay-as-you-wish arrangement, which will not be protected under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Committee wanted to draw a very clear line on situations where the Bill applies as the focus of this Bill is on food donation for a charitable, benevolent and philanthropic purpose.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should also point out that where food donation is to needy families, it is fairly unlikely that the recipients will be asked to pay for the food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NTUC FairPrice also raised a hypothetical situation of a supermarket paying a food surplus management company to redistribute the donated food to the community.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The donation in this scenario will still enjoy liability protections.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is because no payment is received by the supermarket for the food given.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Mr Keith Chua asked how the Committee determined that absolving donors of liability will increase the food available for donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He also asked about the identity of potential donors who are currently reluctant to donate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Committee consulted extensively with restaurants, hotels, social enterprises, primary food producers, food processing companies, distributors, wholesalers, food logistics, transport and delivery provider companies, supermarkets and merchants, bakeries and non-governmental organisations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These stakeholders shared their direct experiences on how liability concerns have a chilling effect on potential food donors, including hotels, restaurants, bakeries and supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This sentiment is echoed by Mr Dellen Soh from the RAS who shared that "Restaurants do want to donate excess food to reduce food waste and help our communities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the very real risk of liability from donated food has a chilling effect for many restaurants." Finally, on this section, Mr Zulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked whether the Bill covers the waiver of liability only in cases of death or personal injury from consuming the donated food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He asked whether illnesses or other physical harms are covered.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For the purposes of this Bill, personal injury includes any disease and any impairment of a person's physical or mental condition.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is similar to the definition adopted under the Civil Law Act, the Limitation Act and the Contributory Negligence and Personal Injuries Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As such, illnesses and physical harms are covered.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will, now, move on to clarifications on the four conditions to enjoy liability protection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also thank Ms Hazel Poa for sharing that these conditions are reasonable and should not pose an excessive impediment to food donors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng spoke about how ensuring donated food is safe and suitable for consumption is a shared responsibility among Government, food donors, community organisations and recipients of food donations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I cannot emphasise enough how this must be a shared responsibility.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also cannot emphasise enough that food safety cannot be compromised.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Food safety was a non-negotiable component in all our consultations and in drafting this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh spoke about how the Bill should not be misused by those with ill intentions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Mr Gan Thiam Poh pointed out, a key challenge is ensuring that the liability protections are appropriately scoped.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After much debate, the Committee came up with the four conditions that I have shared.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the second public consultation, food donation groups asked how it will be determined whether food is unsafe and unsuitable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NTUC FairPrice, similarly, asked whether supermarkets can refer to established standards under food safety legislation to determine safety and suitability for consumption.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, under section 2D of the Sale of Food Act, "food is deemed unsuitable if the food is damaged, deteriorated or perished to an extent that affects its reasonable intended use.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Food is unsuitable if it has packaging that is damaged, deteriorated, perished or contaminated to the extent of affecting the food's reasonable intended use." Existing food safety legislation and case law on food safety will also apply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Keith Chua asked about when recipients might fall ill from consuming donated food, if the food was safe and suitable at the point of donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Despite the best efforts of food donors to ensure that the donated food is safe and suitable, a recipient may still fall ill if the food was not properly handled, not properly stored and not consumed within the appropriate time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: During our consultation, one restaurant owner shared with us that some cleaners had packed leftover food from the restaurant to take home with them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The food had included delicacies, such as prawns.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Seeing how good the food was, the recipient kept the food for the next day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The food likely went bad and the recipient suffered from food poisoning.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After that incident, the restaurant did not dare to allow the leftover food to be packed and taken back.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Of course, in this situation, the restaurant would also have to inform the recipient of the handling requirements and the time limit for consumption and comply with all written laws on food safety and hygiene to enjoy protection from liability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, this is a real story that shows how food that was safe and suitable at the time of donation, might still cause injury not through any fault of the donor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Assoc Prof James Lim referred to the four-hour rule under the NEA guidelines, which limit the consumption time of food from the time it is cooked.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He asked whether the fourth condition, requiring a donor to comply with existing written law on food safety and hygiene, include this four-hour rule.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should clarify that the four-hour rule is not just an NEA guideline.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also suggested that in addition to the four conditions, we should also require that food donors act in good faith in order to enjoy liability protection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I shared, the survey by RAS found that 80% of surveyed restaurants were unsure whether the law will adequately protect businesses, even with the express waiver of liability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Including good faith as a requirement, while it sounds good and I understand where Assoc Prof Jamus Lim is coming from, we feel it might cause even greater concerns for businesses and undermine what the Bill is trying to achieve.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Mr Yip Hon Weng asked for guidelines for donors to follow to prevent unintentional non-compliance with standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He also suggested having resources to be made available on proper handling.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Don Wee and Ms Hany Soh also spoke about having guidelines, best practices and safety standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: SFA has, in 2021, published the Guidelines for Social Service Agencies and community groups involved in food preparation and distribution activities for charitable causes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These guidelines would be relevant in considering if the four conditions for a waiver of liability have been met.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I urge SFA to expand these guidelines to also cover food donors, such as restaurants, hotels and bakeries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will provide them with the much-needed guidance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also urge organisations to familiarise themselves with these very good guidelines and strictly adhere to them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope SFA will also consider doing briefing sessions for food donors to ensure food donors understand the guidelines and clarify any doubts they have.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: SFA should also make these guidelines more easily accessible to the public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As mentioned in my Second Reading speech, complying with these guidelines is one of the conditions to enjoy the waiver of liability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Before I end this section, I should address another point that Mr Keith Chua made about providing guidelines on what can and what cannot be donated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This should actually be included into the SFA guidelines as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: During our consultations with the hotels, some of the hotels actually mentioned that they already have these guidelines on what they will donate and what they will not donate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That could be a good starting point of including this current list into the existing SFA guidelines.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As another example, Food from the Heart also have guidelines on what bread they will accept for donation and what bread they would not accept.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, bread with fillings would not be accepted by Food from the Heart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, we have a starting point in terms of developing guidelines on what can and cannot be donated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim suggested that we consider mandating information labels on donated cooked food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: NTUC FairPrice also asked about the role of packaging and labelling in meeting the conditions on communicating handling requirements and expiry date.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Properly packaging and labelling donated food are examples of how a donor can meet the conditions on communicating handling requirements and time limits for consuming donated food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are other ways that a donor can communicate handling requirements and time limits to recipients.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, they can do so through text messages.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are mindful that mandating labelling might be too onerous for some small donors and we do not want this Bill to have the unintended effect of turning food donors away.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, as the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng had just mentioned in his speech, I understand MSE is considering mandating labelling and I look forward to the Food Safety and Security Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, on this section, Mr Don Wee suggested other methods for ensuring accountability, including maintaining records of donation, requiring reporting on food donation, regular audits and publication of donation data and impact reports.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Don Wee's suggestion on requiring reporting on food donation is a next step that the Government should seriously consider.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a further step, I hope the Government will look into food donation reporting requirements for these big players as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a good suggestion from Mr Don Wee.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government should also look into the suggestion and ideas by Mr Edward Chia about using technology to track and manage food donation more effectively.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Edward Chia gave good examples, which follow on nicely from Mr Don Wee's suggestion.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We intended for these conditions to be reasonable to meet and not any more than what a food donor would already be expected to do before they donate food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Mr Yip Hon Weng pointed out, we need to take a balanced approach on this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, the suggestions that members have raised are all good ideas that MSE, SFA and MSF should look into.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope MSE, SFA and MSF will continue to engage the industry on how they can meet the four conditions and provide the support needed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, I will talk about support and help for our food donors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I fully agree with the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua that food charities augment the support provided by the Government.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Food charities truly embody the spirit of the "many helping hands" approach that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua spoke about.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are our unsung heroes and I thank them for the work they do behind the scenes to ensure that families never go hungry or without nutritious food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Businesses who donate food are equally important too and we should also support them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling spoke about how businesses would like the help of legislation that reduces the fear of liability and reputational damage so that they can meet their societal responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I spoke to many businesses, including restaurants, hotels, bakeries, supermarkets and merchants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I can assure the public that food donation is not just a matter of checking off a corporate social responsibility obligation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of the businesses I spoke with, see food donation as one way of giving back to the community.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The liability protection is one way of helping these businesses and food charities do good.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But as Mr Yip Hon Weng suggested, liability protection essentially removes a barrier but we must now provide active encouragement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Members have raised many good ideas for further incentivising and supporting food donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Miss Rachel Ong, Ms Joan Pereira, Ms Jean See and Ms Hazel Poa suggested tax benefits for food donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also suggested subsidies for logistical costs and Ms Hazel Poa suggested tax incentives for transport or platform companies who assist in providing food pick-up and delivery services for larger F&B enterprises.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng raised examples of tech-enabled inventory management that receives substantial government support and recognition in Japan and Australia.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These were suggestions that were commonly raised during our consultation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We heard from many businesses that some additional financial support from the Government could make it easier for them to donate food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These chillers can be used to quickly freeze cooked food, extending its shelf life beyond the normal four-hour mark and making it easier to donate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many businesses are already doing this and what would help further is to incorporate guidelines on the use of blast chillers into the expanded SFA guidelines that I called for earlier.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These guidelines will help provide some certainty to food donors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Businesses and food charities also shared with us that refrigerated trucks would be very useful for supporting food donations and hope to receive subsidies for purchasing these.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All these suggestions will help food donors and, very importantly, help to ensure safer and more efficient handling of donated food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Another suggestion raised, is tax deduction for donated food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Mr Yip Hon Weng noted, this is currently being done in other countries, including the US and Italy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, there are currently challenges with accurately valuing food for the purpose of tax deduction and preventing any potential abuse.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After exploring these options with the Ministry of Finance, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, MSF and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth, the committee concluded that these financial incentives have to be studied further and can be considered for future implementation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Don Wee and Ms Ng Ling Ling also raised other suggestions, including public recognition programmes for food donors and encouraging food donors to purchase liability insurance as an extra layer of protection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Government will continue to study the possibility of additional support that can be extended to food donors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Charities Food Work Group that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua chairs, may be a good platform for these suggestions to be explored further.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, while liability insurance may be difficult to mandate because it may not be feasible for smaller players.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is scope to explore this option for larger players.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government can take steps to encourage liability insurance and monitor the take-up rate of such insurance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Mr Yip Hon Weng suggested mandatory training programmes or certification for frequent food donors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Don Wee, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Ms Jean See, similarly, suggested training programmes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Committee considered and consulted the public on requiring food charities to be certified, accredited and undergo training.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Smaller groups shared that their volunteer pool may be individuals who volunteer on an ad hoc basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These volunteers may be dissuaded if they have to undergo compulsory training.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The groups also shared that they may not have the resources to meet the accreditation requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That said, voluntary training and certification are steps that may be good for the Charities Food Work Group to explore further.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Government can also provide the much needed assistance on this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Edward Chia had shared about the importance of accreditation and suggested that the Government provide grants to cover costs associated with adopting these standards and conducting necessary training.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: His suggestion of Enterprise Singapore's Quality and Standards division developing a standard specifically tailored to our local context, ensuring it meets the unique needs of our community, should also be looked into.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, on this section, Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about mediation mechanisms and legal assistance for small donors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mediation is always a possibility for civil disputes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As for donors who require legal assistance, there are existing avenues for legal support, including legal clinics for individuals and the Singapore Association of Trade and Commerce, which provides legal support for businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will now talk about support and help for recipients of donated food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Yip asked if the Bill offers legal protection for donors who unintentionally provide food that does not align with a recipient's dietary needs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Keith Chua suggested that we introduce channels of guidance for food-insecure communities to assist them in making the right choices and advising them on their rights.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The usual channels for legal aid and assistance, including the Legal Aid Bureau and Pro Bono SG, are available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On helping food insecure communities to make the right choices, our social service agencies, food charities and Government agencies play an important role in helping those they serve make informed choices while respecting their autonomy to decide for themselves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What Mr Chua suggested is very much needed and public education is key to this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Waiving liability is just one part of the food donation picture.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Miss Rachel Ong spoke about how public education alongside the Bill's implementation is key.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I could not agree more with Miss Ong's point that rescued food is not meant only for the needy, but for all of us.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The rest of society must adopt a similar mindset for food waste reduction efforts in Singapore for it to be significant and effective.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh noted that there is a need for education and understanding, especially over social and cultural norms on food wastage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Don Wee suggested fostering partnerships between donors and reputable charities to ensure proper distribution and use of donated food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Encouraging food donation requires tackling a much broader set of issues than just liability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Ms Poh Li San rightly noted, there is much work to be done after we introduce this Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We will need to encourage businesses and supermarkets to come onboard as examples for other food suppliers and operators.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We will also need to increase the number of volunteers, food collection points, donation drop-off nodes and distribution points.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Stronger partnerships between food rescue groups, Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres will also help in strengthening food donation networks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Mr Edward Chia suggested, the CDCs also have an important role to play in terms of establishing community-based redistribution networks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I feel like I am just shooting arrows here, but the point is that many people have to come onboard this journey for this to be a successful journey.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill is important, but, again, it is just one part of a larger picture.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Government will continue working with businesses and food charities to look into what else we can do to encourage food donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Ms Joan Pereira suggested, the Government should also consider providing the administrative and infrastructural support to help organisations get started on this journey of donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MSF's Food Charities Work Group that I have mentioned many times in this speech is an important platform for such conversations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should add that following this Bill, I will continue to speak up about tackling food waste.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is not the end of my journey.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I promise to continue to file Parliamentary Questions on this and to continue to push the Government to, as always, do more and, before I forget, do more, more quickly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has been an absolutely rewarding four-year journey in drafting this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As Mr Yip Hon Weng pointed out, this Bill can be a catalyst for positive change in how we, as a society, approach food waste and food security.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is about developing a more sustainable and compassionate society.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I sincerely hope we can achieve what Ms Jean See shared in her speech, that this "Bill is the gamechanger that can help to dismantle the stigma surrounding food support while giving food-insecure families the confidence to benefit from food support that is dignified, sustained, adequate and enriching".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Think about not wasting food in the first place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is scary that food waste is so ingrained in our society now.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some of the businesses were telling me that they already factored food waste into their business costs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do not need to worry about throwing food away.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I worked on this Bill, I was constantly reminded of my late grandmother.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Actually, I constantly nag people about not wasting food because my grandmother constantly nagged me when I was young to not waste food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One of my tasks at family meals when I was a little boy was to scoop rice for everyone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I always remember opening the rice cooker and seeing my grandmother's food there.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was always one meal behind the rest of the family.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When we were having dinner, she was having the leftovers from lunch.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After dinner, she stored the leftover food overnight to eat the next day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For her, and for many of our Pioneer Generation, even the smallest scrap of food waste is unthinkable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My grandmother did not even want to waste gas to warm up her food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She warmed up her food using the steam in the rice cooker as we cooked our rice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We now live in a time when food is more abundant as compared to the past.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Most Singaporeans not only have more than enough food available, we are spoilt for choice, with food from all corners of the world being imported into Singapore daily.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I would be glad to answer any further clarifications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us treasure our precious resources and, together, tackle this throwaway culture.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Ng, my grandmother and my mother had exactly the same behaviour as your grandmother.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Looks like, Mr Ng, your wrap-up speech was very, very comprehensive.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 2.57 pm until 3.20 pm.
